goal: Add an opt-in pilot-local lean tool profile without changing task, skill, grader, model, budget or shared-profile behavior.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The native lean catalog exposes exactly the eight retained filesystem, shell, search and skill tools, with goal/todo and unrelated orchestration absent.
The standard profile remains the default with identical patch bytes; security and model services remain unchanged.
Profile source and rendered patch are bound to approval and comparison identities, with observed catalogs validated in new receipts.
Actual headless DSH completes the keyless shell and selected-skill-byte probe under both profiles without provider calls.

outcome.summary: Lean profile implemented and verified. Native tool count falls from twenty-five to eight; logged tool-definition bytes fall from 26686 to 7969. This is catalog and protocol evidence, not measured task improvement or provider-cost savings. No paid run or paid-ledger change.

what_worked: Used inspected row IDs from the pinned installed DSH composition rather than changing DSH core.
Disabled the bash background option alongside job-management tools while preserving filesystem and sandbox services.
Native request headers matched the complete expected catalogs on both profiles.
Full repository gate passed with 1097 tests passing and 7 opt-in tests skipped.
what_failed: An initial context-digest test fixture omitted required context fields and failed closed; the fixture was completed without weakening validation.

evidence.summary: 148 focused tests passed. Full typecheck, build, 51 test files, capsule, policy, offline evaluation and whitespace gates passed; 1097 tests passed and 7 were skipped.
Native lean catalog: eight tools, 7969 logged tool-definition bytes, 1560 system-field bytes. Shell marker and selected-skill digest passed.
Native standard catalog: twenty-five tools, 26686 logged tool-definition bytes, 4148 system-field bytes. Same image, task and skill; shell marker and skill digest passed.

notes: Paid effectiveness remains unmeasured. A lean trial needs a fresh exact approval and sufficient allocation; a cross-profile comparison cannot be labeled skill-only improvement.
